name: Campground
summary: A tent / partial-hookup (water + electric) campground's per-site cost is dominated by the comfort station(s) spread over the sites, the loop roads and parking spurs, and whichever sites get water/electric. Public park projects (state and national parks) run far above private campgrounds because of accessibility upgrades, demolition, remote locations and prevailing wages. Evidence is public-sector bid/estimate data plus thin private data; the default is a derived build-up, confidence medium-low.

typicalSize.method: Judgment from public examples: Tuolumne Meadows 329 sites (c1) is a large national-park campground; Missouri state-park loops are 17-63 sites (rv-park-resort e1-e4). Private campgrounds commonly 30-150 sites.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: RV parks plan ~12.5 sites/acre (Richmond BC, rv-park-resort e20). Tent/partial-hookup campgrounds keep more vegetation and buffers between sites, so ~25% lower (mid 9); low for wooded/primitive layouts.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: One parking spur per site plus overflow/visitor and comfort-station parking; judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Build-up for a 75-site campground, half tent sites and half water/electric sites, one comfort station per ~50 sites. Tent site (graded pad, parking spur, table, fire ring, share of loop road) ~$9k; water/electric site ~$20k (industry estimate $15k-$25k per developed site, c4; Menahga MN full-hookup sites $9.2k materials only, c5); comfort station $0.7M (South Dakota bid $705,540, c2) / 50 sites = ~$14k per site. Mid = 0.5 x 9k + 0.5 x 20k + 14k = $28.5k, rounded to $30k. Low $10k = private primitive campground with vault toilets and gravel roads. High $80k = public-park rehabilitation: Tuolumne Meadows estimate $26.2M / 329 sites = $79.6k per site all-in (c1, 2021); Missouri full-hookup average $55k (rv-park-resort e6, 2020). Evidence years 2020-2025, not escalated by hand.

scope.notes: Per-site contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P: clearing/grading, loop roads and parking spurs, tent pads, water/electric to the partial-hookup sites, on-site water and sewer mains to the comfort station, and the comfort station share. Excludes land, soft costs, site furnishings (FF&E), off-site utilities and on-site wastewater treatment (separate line items).

qualityTiers.method: Economy ~= low/mid (10k/30k = 0.33) tempered to 0.4; luxury ~= high/mid (80k/30k = 2.67) tempered to 2.4 since the high anchor is a public national-park rehab; premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Started from the RV park split (OH Weekly itemization, rv-park-resort e8) and shifted weight: electrical 0.12 -> 0.08 (only half the sites have power), buildings 0.23 -> 0.28 (comfort station is ~45% of the mid build-up; masonry/precast typical in public parks, hence 04 and 22 larger), earthwork up to 0.10 (wooded sites, clearing), roads/pads/site furnishings 0.31, utilities 0.15.

lineItems.name: Comfort station with flush toilets and showers

cost.method: South Dakota Palisades SP comfort station low bid $705,540 (c2, 2023) = mid; Oregon State Parks prototype restroom/shower building $1.1M (c3, 2024) = high; low = smaller/prefab private building (judgment).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out. One per ~40-60 sites; add a second for larger campgrounds.

lineItems.name: Precast vault toilet (double)

cost.method: Planning judgment for a delivered and set precast double vault toilet; no bid tab retrieved in this session. Verify.

lineItems.notes: Used in primitive loops instead of, or in addition to, a comfort station.

lineItems.name: Water + 30/50A electric hookup per partial-hookup site

cost.method: OH Weekly electrical ~$4.0k/site (rv e9) + water lines ~$2.4k/site (rv e8) less ~15% for no sewer trench sharing = ~$5.5k; pedestal hardware $500-$600 (rv e13).

lineItems.notes: Qty 0.5 per site assumes half the sites are partial-hookup.

lineItems.name: Tent pad, parking spur and site grading

cost.method: Judgment: timber-edged gravel tent pad, aggregate spur, grading and erosion control. High = ADA-accessible hardened pads typical of public projects (Tuolumne 'hardened parking pads', c1).
Judgment: one-way 12-14 ft loop (cheaper per LF than RV park two-way roads) with ~50 LF per site given wider site spacing. Verify with site plan.

lineItems.name: RV dump station
lineItems.notes: Common where partial-hookup sites have no sewer.

lineItems.name: Septic system / drainfield for comfort station

cost.method: OH Weekly: small parks have done entire septic for ~$100k (rv e14); campground loads lower than full-hookup RV parks (only the comfort station + dump station), mid $150k.

lineItems.notes: Switch on where no municipal sewer.

lineItems.name: Water well and small public water system

cost.method: Judgment for a prefabricated steel or timber shelter on slab.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Picnic table, fire ring and lantern post per site (~$400-$900); high adds bear-proof food storage locker and accessible table, as specified at Tuolumne (c1). Judgment on prices.

pctOfHard.method: Missouri State Parks design and bidding ~11.4% of construction (rv e18); add permitting/environmental review (NEPA on federal land pushes to the high end).

softCosts.notes: Public projects on federal land carry environmental and cultural-resource review.

design.method: Judgment; concept estimates for park loops often lack survey/geotech.

hard.method: Missouri State Parks carried 15% on concept estimates (rv e19).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min = primitive private campground with vault toilets plus minimal soft costs; max = public-park rehab all-in (Tuolumne $79.6k/site in 2021, c1) with escalation headroom and Missouri small-loop totals ($98k-$118k/site, rv e1/e4).

source.title: Tuolumne Meadows Campground in Yosemite National Park To Be Repaired and Improved through GAOA Funding

evidence.quote: Project Costs: Approximately $26.2 million (estimate); 'This $20 million dollar project will rehabilitate the 329-site Tuolumne Meadows Campground, including walk-in...'
evidence.scopeNotes: Value = $26.2M / 329 sites. The page states both $20M and ~$26.2M; the later estimate used. Scope: comfort stations modernized/added, roads and culverts, hardened parking pads, tables, fire rings, food lockers, water and sewer systems, relocation of sites from riverbanks. Contract awarded Sept 15, 2021. Remote high-elevation site; total project cost, not hard cost only.
